title: Sita goes home to the earth
hookLine: Sita's last oath, and why Hindus say her name before Rama's
carry: sita is a goddess, named before rama
tomorrow: the poets loved this story. did they keep her ending?
last: TWO BOYS SING TO THEIR FATHER.

lines: ASKED ONCE MORE TO PROVE HERSELF.
cards: Sita's name means furrow. Back in the first book, King Janaka was plowing a field for a ritual when the plow turned up a baby girl in the earth. He raised her as his daughter and named her for the furrow.
Hold on to that, because the Ramayana remembers it. Today the girl from the furrow, now the mother of two grown boys, is brought before a great assembly and asked, one more time, to prove herself.

teach.h: LET HER SWEAR IT BEFORE EVERYONE.
teach.b: When Rama learns the singing boys are his sons, he sends word to Valmiki: if Sita is pure, let her come and swear it here, before everyone. The next morning the assembly fills: sages, kings, ordinary people.
Valmiki walks in first, and Sita follows, head bowed. These are your sons, Valmiki tells Rama, and Sita is blameless; he stakes on it all the merit of his long life.
Rama answers that he believes it, and that he sent her away because of what people were saying. But the oath is still asked of her. Then Sita speaks.

teach.h: IF I HAVE NEVER THOUGHT OF ANOTHER.
teach.b: If I have never thought of anyone but Rama, let the earth goddess open and give me a place. If I have honored him in mind, word and deed, let the earth receive me. The ground splits.

teach.h: THE EARTH OPENS AND TAKES HER HOME.
teach.b: A shining throne rises, held up by serpents, and the earth goddess takes Sita in her arms and seats her there. The throne sinks, and the earth closes. Rama is wild with grief.
The girl from the furrow has gone home to her mother. Now, here's what Hindus did with that ending.

They didn't remember Sita as a woman who lost. They worship her. Many honor her as Lakshmi, the goddess, come down beside Vishnu's avatar, and in the Ram darbar picture in many homes she sits at Rama's side.
Listen to how people greet each other in much of North India: Sita Ram, or Jai Siya Ram.

teach.h: JAI SIYA RAM: HER NAME FIRST.
teach.b: Her name comes first, the way devotees also say Radha Krishna and Gauri Shankar. Many explain it simply: the Goddess, the mother, is named first.

how: Sita's return to the earth is told in Hindu homes, songs and stage plays, often with deep grief for her; devotees honor Sita as a goddess in her own right, linked with the earth and with Lakshmi, and many greet each other with 'Sita Ram' or 'Jai Siya Ram', her name first.

o: her name means furrow, the earth she was found in
her name means faithful wife, the one who waits
her name means moonlight, for her calm beauty

p: takes her onto a rising throne

s: in 'Jai Siya Ram', Sita's name comes before Rama's
many devotees explain it: the Goddess, the mother, is named first, as in Radha Krishna.
Sita refuses to speak at the assembly
she makes solemn declarations: if she has never thought of another, let the earth receive her.
Rama is calm when the earth takes her
the text shows him overwhelmed with grief.

games.q: a friend hears an auntie greet someone with 'jai siya ram' and asks why Sita's name comes first if Rama's the hero. what fits today?
o: many Hindus honor Sita as a goddess, Lakshmi beside Vishnu's avatar, so she's named first.
it's just easier to say that way round.
it's because people are angry at Rama for sending her away.
games.why: the earth's daughter isn't remembered as the one who lost. she's worshiped, and in Sita Ram her name comes first.

practice: If you can, put your bare feet flat on the ground, or sit on the floor, and feel your weight handed down into the earth. The ground is holding you. If you pray, say Sita Ram softly on each out-breath, to the earth's daughter.
If you don't, just thank the ground for holding you up.

wordCard.voice: Sita. Her name means furrow: found in the earth, gone home to it, and honored as a goddess, named first whenever people say Sita Ram.

orig.note: Sanskrit sītā: the furrow a plow makes. Sita was found in one, and goes back into the earth.

carryVoice: Your line: Sita is a goddess, named before Rama. Tomorrow, the poets who couldn't let her ending go. Day six hundred sixty-six, done.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 66 (Janaka finds Sita while plowing)
